caveats: Source is ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer's 'Full Filing' render of the IRS e-file XML for the Form 990 (same IRS object IDs as on IRS TEOS). The raw XML download link on ProPublica returned an HTTP 403 'Security Check' page to curl (a ProPublica bot check, not the egress proxy); I did not try to bypass it and used the site's openly served rendered pages instead. The IRS TEOS XML was not separately pulled. Part IX sits on page 10 of the Form 990 (the render's page header 'Form 990 (2024) Page 10' precedes Part IX for FY25; 'Form 990 (2023) Page 10' and '(2022) Page 10' for FY24 and FY23).

Tax-year labels: the IRS form is labelled by the calendar year in which the tax year begins. 'TY 2024 Form 990' = July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025 = FY25 (submitted 2026-05-15). 'TY 2023' = FY24 (submitted 2025-05-14). 'TY 2022' = FY23 (submitted 2024-05-15). Beginning and ending dates were read from the header of each return. ProPublica also lists separate Form 990-T filings for each year; those were not used.
Column sums check: for every line read, column A equals B + C + D in all three years.

Scope difference: the 990 is filed by Northeastern University (Boston, EIN 04-1679980). Part IV lines 12a and 12b of the FY25 990 show it obtained no separate audit (12a No) and was included in consolidated independent audited statements (12b Yes). The audited statements consolidate subsidiaries (Kostas Research Institute, New College of the Humanities UK and, from June 16, 2025, Marymount Manhattan College). Plausible reasons the 990 S&B is below the audited line are entities and campuses outside the 990 filer, plus accrual/timing and classification differences (for example pension accruals in 990 line 8 versus audited expense); the filings do not itemize the gap, so no cause is asserted.

The 990 total expenses (line 25) are far above audited total operating expenses because the 990 counts scholarship aid gross (line 2, $641.0M FY25) while the audited statements net financial aid ($642.5M FY25) against tuition revenue. After removing line 2 the FY25 gap is small (see reconciliation).

Interest and D&A corroboration (bonus, from Part IX lines 20 and 22): 990 interest ($49.4M FY25) is within about 1% of the audited operating Interest line ($49.9M), which supports using the operating-expense Interest line (and not the $60.0M debt-note figure) in the core opex calculation. 990 D&A ($145.5M) is about 3.8% below audited Depreciation ($151.25M) in FY25.

No estimate is applied: the S&W ratio is reported for stability only. To carry S&W into the audited framework the audited 'Salary and benefits' line would have to be split, which neither source does; the 990 S&W (lines 5+6+7) is the directly reported number; the 990 lines 5-10 total is 3.2% to 3.4% below audited Salary and benefits in each of the three years.
stability_summary: S&W share of (lines 5-10): FY23 82.07%, FY24 81.63%, FY25 80.54%; range 1.53 points. 990 lines 5-10 vs audited Salary and benefits: FY23 -3.42%, FY24 -3.43%, FY25 -3.24%.
